_meta.title: Modern Standard Arabic
_meta.description: Everyday and formal Arabic (Fusha) vocabulary: the script, how it sounds and what it means.

msa-e-1.question: What does the Arabic word مَرْحَبًا (pronounced marḥaban) mean?
msa-e-1.explanation: مَرْحَبًا (marḥaban) means “Hello / Welcome”. Marhaban (مرحباً) is the standard greeting used across the Arab world. Practical example: 'Marhaban ya sadiqi' (Hello my friend / مرحباً يا صديقي).

msa-e-2.question: What does the Arabic word شُكْرًا (pronounced shukran) mean?
msa-e-2.explanation: شُكْرًا (shukran) means “Thank you”. Shukran (شكراً) means thank you. Practical example: 'Shukran jazilan ala musa'adatik' (Thank you very much for your help / شكراً جزيلاً على مساعدتك).

msa-e-3.question: What does the Arabic word مِنْ فَضْلِك (pronounced min faḍlik) mean?
msa-e-3.explanation: مِنْ فَضْلِك (min faḍlik) means “Please”. Min fadlik (من فضلك) means 'please' (literally: from your favor). Practical example: 'A'tini al-ma' min fadlik' (Give me water, please / أعطني الماء من فضلك).

msa-e-4.question: What does the Arabic word صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر (pronounced ṣabāḥ al-khayr) mean?
msa-e-4.explanation: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر (ṣabāḥ al-khayr) means “Good morning”. Sabah al-khayr (صباح الخير) means good morning, and the typical reply is 'Sabah an-nur'. Practical example: 'Sabah al-khayr ya ustadhi' (Good morning, my teacher).

msa-e-5.question: What does the Arabic word كِتَاب (pronounced kitāb) mean?
msa-e-5.explanation: كِتَاب (kitāb) means “Book”. Kitab (كتاب) means book (plural: Kutub). Practical example: 'haadha kitabun jadeed' (This is a new book / هذا كتاب جديد).

msa-e-6.question: What does the Arabic word قَلَم (pronounced qalam) mean?
options: Out of caution / as a precautionary measure
msa-e-6.explanation: قَلَم (qalam) means “Pen or pencil”. Qalam is used for any writing instrument. Practical example: 'Aktubu al-dars bil-qalam' (I write the lesson with the pen / أكتب الدرس بالقلم).

msa-e-7.question: What does the Arabic word بَيْت (pronounced bayt) mean?
msa-e-7.explanation: بَيْت (bayt) means “House / Home”. Bayt (بيت) means house or home. Practical example: 'Ana fi al-bayt' (I am at home / أنا في البيت).

msa-e-8.question: What does the Arabic word مَاء (pronounced māʾ) mean?
msa-e-8.explanation: مَاء (māʾ) means “Water”. Ma' (ماء) means water. Practical example: 'Uridu sharb al-ma'' (I want to drink water / أريد شرب الماء).

msa-e-9.question: What does the Arabic word نَعَمْ (pronounced naʿam) mean?
msa-e-9.explanation: نَعَمْ (naʿam) means “Yes”. Na'am is the affirmative particle 'yes'. Practical example: 'Na'am, ana a'rifu dhalika' (Yes, I know that / نعم، أنا أعرف ذلك).

msa-e-10.question: What does the Arabic word لَا (pronounced lā) mean?
msa-e-10.explanation: لَا (lā) means “No”. La is the negation particle 'no'. Practical example: 'La, shukran' (No, thank you / لا، شكراً).

msa-e-11.question: What does the Arabic word مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر (pronounced masāʾ al-khayr) mean?
msa-e-11.explanation: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر (masāʾ al-khayr) means “Good evening”. Masa' al-khayr (مساء الخير) means good evening. Practical example: 'Masa' al-khayr ya zumaala'i' (Good evening, my colleagues / مساء الخير يا زملائي).

msa-e-12.question: What does the Arabic word مَدْرَسَة (pronounced madrasah) mean?
msa-e-12.explanation: مَدْرَسَة (madrasah) means “School”. Madrasah (مدرسة) means school. Practical example: 'Al-walad yadhhabu ila al-madrasah' (The boy goes to school / الولد يذهب إلى المدرسة).

msa-e-13.question: What does the Arabic word شَارِع (pronounced shāriʿ) mean?
msa-e-13.explanation: شَارِع (shāriʿ) means “Street / Road”. Shari' means street. Practical example: 'Bayti fi hadha al-shari'' (My house is on this street / بيتي في هذا الشارع).

msa-e-14.question: What does the Arabic word سَيَّارَة (pronounced sayyārah) mean?
msa-e-14.explanation: سَيَّارَة (sayyārah) means “Car”. Sayarah (سيارة) means car. Practical example: 'Ishtaraytu sayarah jadeedah' (I bought a new car / اشتريت سيارة جديدة).

msa-e-15.question: What does the Arabic word مَعَ السَّلَامَة (pronounced maʿa as-salāmah) mean?
msa-e-15.explanation: مَعَ السَّلَامَة (maʿa as-salāmah) means “Goodbye”. Ma'a as-salama (مع السلامة) means go with safety / goodbye. Practical example: 'Ila al-liqa', ma'a as-salama' (Until we meet, goodbye / إلى اللقاء، مع السلامة).

msa-e-16.question: What does the Arabic word صَدِيق (pronounced ṣadīq) mean?
msa-e-16.explanation: صَدِيق (ṣadīq) means “Friend”. Sadiq means friend. Practical example: 'Muhammad sadiqi al-mufaddal' (Muhammad is my favorite friend / محمد صديقي المفضل).

msa-e-17.question: What does the Arabic word طَعَام (pronounced ṭaʿām) mean?
msa-e-17.explanation: طَعَام (ṭaʿām) means “Food / Meal”. Ta'am (طعام) means food. Practical example: 'Al-ta'am ladhidh jiddan' (The food is very delicious / الطعام لذيذ جداً).

msa-e-18.question: What does the Arabic word بَاب (pronounced bāb) mean?
msa-e-18.explanation: بَاب (bāb) means “Door”. Bab means door. Practical example: 'Iftah al-bab min fadlik' (Open the door, please / افتح الباب من فضلك).

msa-e-19.question: What does the Arabic word شَمْس (pronounced shams) mean?
msa-e-19.explanation: شَمْس (shams) means “Sun”. Shams (شمس) means sun. Practical example: 'Al-shams tushriqu kulla sabah' (The sun shines every morning / الشمس تشرق كل صباح).

msa-e-20.question: What does the Arabic word قَمَر (pronounced qamar) mean?
msa-e-20.explanation: قَمَر (qamar) means “Moon”. Qamar means moon. Practical example: 'Al-qamar jamilun al-laylah' (The moon is beautiful tonight / القمر جميل الليلة).

msa-e-21.question: What does the Arabic word كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (pronounced kayfa ḥāluka) mean?
msa-e-21.explanation: كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (kayfa ḥāluka) means “How are you? (to a male)”. Kayfa haluka (كيف حالك؟) asks how are you. Practical example: 'Kayfa haluka ya akhi?' (How are you, my brother? / كيف حالك يا أخي?).

msa-e-22.question: What does the Arabic word اسْم (pronounced ism) mean?
msa-e-22.explanation: اسْم (ism) means “Name”. Ism means name. Practical example: 'Ma ismuka?' (What is your name? / ما اسمك?).

msa-e-23.question: What does the Arabic word الْيَوْم (pronounced al-yawm) mean?
msa-e-23.explanation: الْيَوْم (al-yawm) means “Today”. Al-yawm (اليوم) means today. Practical example: 'Al-yawm al-jaww jamil' (Today the weather is nice / اليوم الجو جميل).

msa-e-24.question: What does the Arabic word غَدًا (pronounced ghadan) mean?
msa-e-24.explanation: غَدًا (ghadan) means “Tomorrow”. Ghadan means tomorrow. Practical example: 'Sanusaafiru ghadan in sha Allah' (We will travel tomorrow, God willing / سنسافر غداً إن شاء الله).

msa-e-25.question: What does the Arabic word سُوق (pronounced sūq) mean?
msa-e-25.explanation: سُوق (sūq) means “Market / Store”. Suq (سوق) means market. Practical example: 'Dhahabtu ila al-suq li-shira' al-khudar' (I went to the market to buy vegetables / ذهبت إلى السوق لشراء الخضار).

msa-e-26.question: What does the Arabic word بَيْت كَبِير (pronounced bayt kabīr) mean?
msa-e-26.explanation: بَيْت كَبِير (bayt kabīr) means “Big house”. Kabir means big. Practical example: 'Hum yaskununa fi baytin kabir' (They live in a big house / هم يسكنون في بيت كبير).

msa-e-27.question: What does the Arabic word تُفَّاح (pronounced tuffāḥ) mean?
msa-e-27.explanation: تُفَّاح (tuffāḥ) means “Apple”. Tuffah (تفاح) means apple. Practical example: 'Uhibbu akal al-tuffah' (I like eating apples / أكل التفاح).

msa-e-28.question: What does the Arabic word جَمِيل (pronounced jamīl) mean?
msa-e-28.explanation: جَمِيل (jamīl) means “Beautiful / Nice”. Jamil means beautiful or nice. Practical example: 'Hadhihi madiNah jamilah' (This is a beautiful city / هذه مدينة جميلة).

msa-e-29.question: What does the Arabic word لُغَة (pronounced lughah) mean?
msa-e-29.explanation: لُغَة (lughah) means “Language”. Lughah (لغة) means language. Practical example: 'Al-lughah al-arabiyyah jamilah' (The Arabic language is beautiful / اللغة العربية جميلة).

msa-e-30.question: What does the Arabic word كَبِير (pronounced kabīr) mean?
msa-e-30.explanation: كَبِير (kabīr) means “Big / Large”. Kabir means big. Practical example: 'Al-maktabah kabiratan' (The library is large / المكتبة كبيرة).

msa-e-31.question: What does the Arabic word صَغِير (pronounced ṣaghīr) mean?
msa-e-31.explanation: صَغِير (ṣaghīr) means “Small”. Saghir (صغير) means small. Practical example: 'Hadha waladun saghir' (This is a small boy / هذا ولد صغير).

msa-e-32.question: What does the Arabic word أُحِبُّ (pronounced uḥibbu) mean?
msa-e-32.explanation: أُحِبُّ (uḥibbu) means “I love / I like”. Uhibbu (أحب) means I love / like. Practical example: 'Uhibbu qira'at al-kutub' (I love reading books / أحب قراءة الكتب).

msa-e-33.question: What does the Arabic word أُرِيدُ (pronounced urīdu) mean?
msa-e-33.explanation: أُرِيدُ (urīdu) means “I want”. Uridu means I want. Practical example: 'Uridu qahwah min fadlik' (I want coffee, please / أريد قهوة من فضلك).

msa-e-34.question: What does the Arabic word حَلِيب (pronounced ḥalīb) mean?
msa-e-34.explanation: حَلِيب (ḥalīb) means “Milk”. Halib (حليب) means milk. Practical example: 'Al-atfal yashrabuna al-halib' (Children drink milk / الأطفال يشربون الحليب).

msa-e-35.question: What does the Arabic word وَاحِد (pronounced wāḥid) mean?
msa-e-35.explanation: وَاحِد (wāḥid) means “one”. Practical example: ‘ʿindī kitāb wāḥid’ (I have one book / عندي كتاب واحد).

msa-e-36.question: What does the Arabic word اِثْنَان (pronounced ithnān) mean?
msa-e-36.explanation: اِثْنَان (ithnān) means “two”. Practical example: ‘lahu waladān ithnān’ (He has two sons / له ولدان اثنان).

msa-e-37.question: What does the Arabic word ثَلَاثَة (pronounced thalāthah) mean?
msa-e-37.explanation: ثَلَاثَة (thalāthah) means “three”. Practical example: ‘thalāthatu ayyām’ (three days / ثلاثة أيام).

msa-e-38.question: What does the Arabic word أَرْبَعَة (pronounced arbaʿah) mean?
msa-e-38.explanation: أَرْبَعَة (arbaʿah) means “four”. Practical example: ‘arbaʿatu kutub’ (four books / أربعة كتب).

msa-e-39.question: What does the Arabic word خَمْسَة (pronounced khamsah) mean?
msa-e-39.explanation: خَمْسَة (khamsah) means “five”. Practical example: ‘khamsatu qurūsh’ (five piastres / خمسة قروش).

msa-e-40.question: What does the Arabic word عَشَرَة (pronounced ʿasharah) mean?
msa-e-40.explanation: عَشَرَة (ʿasharah) means “ten”. Practical example: ‘ʿasharatu rijāl’ (ten men / عشرة رجال).

msa-e-41.question: What does the Arabic word مِائَة (pronounced miʾah) mean?
msa-e-41.explanation: مِائَة (miʾah) means “hundred”. Practical example: ‘miʾatu kitāb’ (a hundred books / مائة كتاب).

msa-e-42.question: What does the Arabic word أَلْف (pronounced alf) mean?
msa-e-42.explanation: أَلْف (alf) means “thousand”. Practical example: ‘alf shukr’ (a thousand thanks / ألف شكر).

msa-e-43.question: What does the Arabic word أَحْمَر (pronounced aḥmar) mean?
msa-e-43.explanation: أَحْمَر (aḥmar) means “red”. Practical example: ‘al-wardu aḥmar’ (the rose is red / الورد أحمر).

msa-e-44.question: What does the Arabic word أَزْرَق (pronounced azraq) mean?
msa-e-44.explanation: أَزْرَق (azraq) means “blue”. Practical example: ‘as-samāʾu zarqāʾ’ (the sky is blue / السماء زرقاء).

msa-e-45.question: What does the Arabic word أَخْضَر (pronounced akhḍar) mean?
msa-e-45.explanation: أَخْضَر (akhḍar) means “green”. Practical example: ‘al-ʿushbu akhḍar’ (the grass is green / العشب أخضر).

msa-e-46.question: What does the Arabic word أَصْفَر (pronounced aṣfar) mean?
msa-e-46.explanation: أَصْفَر (aṣfar) means “yellow”. Practical example: ‘at-tuffāḥu aṣfar’ (the apple is yellow / التفاح أصفر).

msa-e-47.question: What does the Arabic word أَبْيَض (pronounced abyaḍ) mean?
msa-e-47.explanation: أَبْيَض (abyaḍ) means “white”. Practical example: ‘al-qamīṣu abyaḍ’ (the shirt is white / القميص أبيض).

msa-e-48.question: What does the Arabic word أَسْوَد (pronounced aswad) mean?
msa-e-48.explanation: أَسْوَد (aswad) means “black”. Practical example: ‘al-laylu aswad’ (the night is black / الليل أسود).

msa-e-49.question: What does the Arabic word أَب (pronounced ab) mean?
msa-e-49.explanation: أَب (ab) means “father”. Practical example: ‘abī ṭabīb’ (my father is a doctor / أبي طبيب).

msa-e-50.question: What does the Arabic word أُمّ (pronounced umm) mean?
msa-e-50.explanation: أُمّ (umm) means “mother”. Practical example: ‘ummī ṭabībah’ (my mother is a doctor / أمي طبيبة).

msa-e-51.question: What does the Arabic word أَخ (pronounced akh) mean?
msa-e-51.explanation: أَخ (akh) means “brother”. Practical example: ‘akhī kabīr’ (my brother is older / أخي كبير).

msa-e-52.question: What does the Arabic word أُخْت (pronounced ukht) mean?
msa-e-52.explanation: أُخْت (ukht) means “sister”. Practical example: ‘ukhtī ṭālibah’ (my sister is a student / أختي طالبة).

msa-e-53.question: What does the Arabic word اِبْن (pronounced ibn) mean?
msa-e-53.explanation: اِبْن (ibn) means “son”. Practical example: ‘ibnī fī al-madrasah’ (my son is at school / ابني في المدرسة).

msa-e-54.question: What does the Arabic word بِنْت (pronounced bint) mean?
msa-e-54.explanation: بِنْت (bint) means “daughter” or “girl”. Practical example: ‘bintī ṣaghīrah’ (my daughter is young / بنتي صغيرة).

msa-e-55.question: What does the Arabic word رَجُل (pronounced rajul) mean?
msa-e-55.explanation: رَجُل (rajul) means “man”. Practical example: ‘ar-rajulu ṭawīl’ (the man is tall / الرجل طويل).

msa-e-56.question: What does the Arabic word اِمْرَأَة (pronounced imraʾah) mean?
msa-e-56.explanation: اِمْرَأَة (imraʾah) means “woman”. Practical example: ‘al-marʾatu ṭabībah’ (the woman is a doctor / المرأة طبيبة).

msa-e-57.question: What does the Arabic word طِفْل (pronounced ṭifl) mean?
msa-e-57.explanation: طِفْل (ṭifl) means “child”. Practical example: ‘aṭ-ṭiflu yanāmu’ (the child is sleeping / الطفل ينام).

msa-e-58.question: What does the Arabic word صَدِيقَة (pronounced ṣadīqah) mean?
msa-e-58.explanation: صَدِيقَة (ṣadīqah) means “female friend”. Practical example: ‘ṣadīqatī fī al-jāmiʿah’ (my friend is at university / صديقتي في الجامعة).

msa-e-59.question: What does the Arabic word رَأْس (pronounced raʾs) mean?
msa-e-59.explanation: رَأْس (raʾs) means “head”. Practical example: ‘raʾsī yuʾlimunī’ (my head hurts / رأسي يؤلمني).

msa-e-60.question: What does the Arabic word عَيْن (pronounced ʿayn) mean?
msa-e-60.explanation: عَيْن (ʿayn) means “eye”. Practical example: ‘ʿaynāhu zarqāwān’ (his eyes are blue / عيناه زرقاوان).

msa-e-61.question: What does the Arabic word يَد (pronounced yad) mean?
msa-e-61.explanation: يَد (yad) means “hand”. Practical example: ‘yadī al-yumnā’ (my right hand / يدي اليمنى).

msa-e-62.question: What does the Arabic word رِجْل (pronounced rijl) mean?
msa-e-62.explanation: رِجْل (rijl) means “foot” or “leg”. Practical example: ‘rijlī al-yusrā’ (my left foot / رجلي اليسرى).

msa-e-63.question: What does the Arabic word قَلْب (pronounced qalb) mean?
msa-e-63.explanation: قَلْب (qalb) means “heart”. Practical example: ‘qalbī yuḥibbu al-khayr’ (my heart loves goodness / قلبي يحب الخير).

msa-e-64.question: What does the Arabic word خُبْز (pronounced khubz) mean?
msa-e-64.explanation: خُبْز (khubz) means “bread”. Practical example: ‘urīdu khubzan ṭāzajan’ (I want fresh bread / أريد خبزاً طازجاً).

msa-e-65.question: What does the Arabic word لَحْم (pronounced laḥm) mean?
msa-e-65.explanation: لَحْم (laḥm) means “meat”. Practical example: ‘lā ākulu al-laḥm’ (I do not eat meat / لا آكل اللحم).

msa-e-66.question: What does the Arabic word سَمَك (pronounced samak) mean?
msa-e-66.explanation: سَمَك (samak) means “fish”. Practical example: ‘as-samaku ṭāzaj’ (the fish is fresh / السمك طازج).

msa-e-67.question: What does the Arabic word دَجَاج (pronounced dajāj) mean?
msa-e-67.explanation: دَجَاج (dajāj) means “chicken”. Practical example: ‘nākulu ad-dajāj al-yawm’ (we are eating chicken today / نأكل الدجاج اليوم).

msa-e-68.question: What does the Arabic word بَيْض (pronounced bayḍ) mean?
msa-e-68.explanation: بَيْض (bayḍ) means “eggs”. Practical example: ‘bayḍatāni li-l-ifuṭār’ (two eggs for breakfast / بيضتان للإفطار).

msa-e-69.question: What does the Arabic word جُبْن (pronounced jubn) mean?
msa-e-69.explanation: جُبْن (jubn) means “cheese”. Practical example: ‘uḥibbu al-jubn’ (I love cheese / أحب الجبن).

msa-e-70.question: What does the Arabic word فَاكِهَة (pronounced fākihah) mean?
msa-e-70.explanation: فَاكِهَة (fākihah) means “fruit”. Practical example: ‘al-fākihah ṣiḥḥiyyah’ (fruit is healthy / الفاكهة صحية).

msa-e-71.question: What does the Arabic word خُضْرَة (pronounced khuḍrah) mean?
msa-e-71.explanation: خُضْرَة (khuḍrah) means “vegetable” / greens. Practical example: ‘ākulū al-khuḍrawāt’ (eat the vegetables / اكلوا الخضروات).

msa-e-72.question: What does the Arabic word شَاي (pronounced shāy) mean?
msa-e-72.explanation: شَاي (shāy) means “tea”. Practical example: ‘hal turīdu shāyan?’ (Do you want tea? / هل تريد شاياً؟).

msa-e-73.question: What does the Arabic word قَهْوَة (pronounced qahwah) mean?
msa-e-73.explanation: قَهْوَة (qahwah) means “coffee”. Practical example: ‘qahwah sūdāʾ min faḍlik’ (black coffee, please / قهوة سوداء من فضلك).

msa-e-74.question: What does the Arabic word عَصِير (pronounced ʿaṣīr) mean?
msa-e-74.explanation: عَصِير (ʿaṣīr) means “juice”. Practical example: ‘ʿaṣīr burtuqāl’ (orange juice / عصير برتقال).

msa-e-75.question: What does the Arabic word مَسْجِد (pronounced masjid) mean?
msa-e-75.explanation: مَسْجِد (masjid) means “mosque”. Practical example: ‘adhhabu ilā al-masjid’ (I go to the mosque / أذهب إلى المسجد).

msa-e-76.question: What does the Arabic word مَطْعَم (pronounced maṭʿam) mean?
msa-e-76.explanation: مَطْعَم (maṭʿam) means “restaurant”. Practical example: ‘natanāwalu al-ghadāʾ fī al-maṭʿam’ (we have lunch at the restaurant / نتناول الغداء في المطعم).

msa-e-77.question: What does the Arabic word فُنْدُق (pronounced funduq) mean?
msa-e-77.explanation: فُنْدُق (funduq) means “hotel”. Practical example: ‘nazaltu fī funduq kabīr’ (I stayed in a large hotel / نزلت في فندق كبير).

msa-e-78.question: What does the Arabic word مَكْتَب (pronounced maktab) mean?
msa-e-78.explanation: مَكْتَب (maktab) means “office” or “desk”. Practical example: ‘aʿmalu fī al-maktab’ (I work in the office / أعمل في المكتب).

msa-e-79.question: What does the Arabic word غُرْفَة (pronounced ghurfah) mean?
msa-e-79.explanation: غُرْفَة (ghurfah) means “room”. Practical example: ‘ghurfatī kabīrah’ (my room is big / غرفتي كبيرة).

msa-e-80.question: What does the Arabic word مَطْبَخ (pronounced maṭbakh) mean?
msa-e-80.explanation: مَطْبَخ (maṭbakh) means “kitchen”. Practical example: ‘aṭbukhu fī al-maṭbakh’ (I cook in the kitchen / أطبخ في المطبخ).

msa-e-81.question: What does the Arabic word حَمَّام (pronounced ḥammām) mean?
msa-e-81.explanation: حَمَّام (ḥammām) means “bathroom”. Practical example: ‘ayna al-ḥammām?’ (Where is the bathroom? / أين الحمام؟).

msa-e-82.question: What does the Arabic word حَدِيقَة (pronounced ḥadīqah) mean?
msa-e-82.explanation: حَدِيقَة (ḥadīqah) means “garden”. Practical example: ‘al-ḥadīqah jamīlah’ (the garden is beautiful / الحديقة جميلة).

msa-e-83.question: What does the Arabic word شَاطِئ (pronounced shāṭiʾ) mean?
msa-e-83.explanation: شَاطِئ (shāṭiʾ) means “beach”. Practical example: ‘nadhhabu ilā ash-shāṭiʾ’ (we go to the beach / نذهب إلى الشاطئ).

msa-e-84.question: What does the Arabic word جَبَل (pronounced jabal) mean?
msa-e-84.explanation: جَبَل (jabal) means “mountain”. Practical example: ‘jabalu Uhud’ (Mount Uhud / جبل أحد).

msa-e-85.question: What does the Arabic word بَحْر (pronounced baḥr) mean?
msa-e-85.explanation: بَحْر (baḥr) means “sea”. Practical example: ‘al-baḥru al-aḥmar’ (the Red Sea / البحر الأحمر).

msa-e-86.question: What does the Arabic word نَهْر (pronounced nahr) mean?
msa-e-86.explanation: نَهْر (nahr) means “river”. Practical example: ‘nahr an-Nīl’ (the Nile River / نهر النيل).

msa-e-87.question: What does the Arabic word سَاعَة (pronounced sāʿah) mean?
msa-e-87.explanation: سَاعَة (sāʿah) means “hour”, “clock” or “watch”. Practical example: ‘as-sāʿatu al-ʿāshirah’ (ten o’clock / الساعة العاشرة).

msa-e-88.question: What does the Arabic word دَقِيقَة (pronounced daqīqah) mean?
msa-e-88.explanation: دَقِيقَة (daqīqah) means “minute”. Practical example: ‘daqīqatān min faḍlik’ (two minutes, please / دقيقتان من فضلك).

msa-e-89.question: What does the Arabic word أُسْبُوع (pronounced usbūʿ) mean?
msa-e-89.explanation: أُسْبُوع (usbūʿ) means “week”. Practical example: ‘fī al-usbūʿ al-qādim’ (next week / في الأسبوع القادم).

msa-e-90.question: What does the Arabic word شَهْر (pronounced shahr) mean?
msa-e-90.explanation: شَهْر (shahr) means “month”. Practical example: ‘shahru Ramaḍān’ (the month of Ramadan / شهر رمضان).

msa-e-91.question: What does the Arabic word سَنَة (pronounced sanah) mean?
msa-e-91.explanation: سَنَة (sanah) means “year”. Practical example: ‘as-sanatu al-jadīdah’ (the new year / السنة الجديدة).

msa-e-92.question: What does the Arabic word طَقْس (pronounced ṭaqs) mean?
msa-e-92.explanation: طَقْس (ṭaqs) means “weather”. Practical example: ‘kayfa aṭ-ṭaqsu al-yawm?’ (How is the weather today? / كيف الطقس اليوم؟).

msa-e-93.question: What does the Arabic word حَارّ (pronounced ḥārr) mean?
msa-e-93.explanation: حَارّ (ḥārr) means “hot”. Practical example: ‘al-jawwu ḥārr’ (the weather is hot / الجو حار).

msa-e-94.question: What does the Arabic word بَارِد (pronounced bārid) mean?
msa-e-94.explanation: بَارِد (bārid) means “cold”. Practical example: ‘al-māʾu bārid’ (the water is cold / الماء بارد).

msa-e-95.question: What does the Arabic word مَطَر (pronounced maṭar) mean?
msa-e-95.explanation: مَطَر (maṭar) means “rain”. Practical example: ‘yumṭiru al-yawm’ (it is raining today / يمطر اليوم).

msa-e-96.question: What does the Arabic word ثَلْج (pronounced thalj) mean?
msa-e-96.explanation: ثَلْج (thalj) means “snow”. Practical example: ‘ath-thalju yatasāqaṭu’ (the snow is falling / الثلج يتساقط).

msa-e-97.question: What does the Arabic word ذَهَبَ (pronounced dhahaba) mean?
msa-e-97.explanation: ذَهَبَ (dhahaba) means “he went”. Practical example: ‘dhahaba ilā al-madrasah’ (he went to school / ذهب إلى المدرسة).

msa-e-98.question: What does the Arabic word جَاءَ (pronounced jāʾa) mean?
msa-e-98.explanation: جَاءَ (jāʾa) means “he came”. Practical example: ‘jāʾa al-ḍayfu’ (the guest came / جاء الضيف).

msa-e-99.question: What does the Arabic word أَكَلَ (pronounced akala) mean?
msa-e-99.explanation: أَكَلَ (akala) means “he ate”. Practical example: ‘akala at-tuffāḥah’ (he ate the apple / أكل التفاحة).

msa-e-100.question: What does the Arabic word شَرِبَ (pronounced shariba) mean?
msa-e-100.explanation: شَرِبَ (shariba) means “he drank”. Practical example: ‘shariba al-māʾ’ (he drank the water / شرب الماء).

msa-e-101.question: What does the Arabic word قَرَأَ (pronounced qaraʾa) mean?
msa-e-101.explanation: قَرَأَ (qaraʾa) means “he read”. Practical example: ‘qaraʾa al-kitāb’ (he read the book / قرأ الكتاب).

msa-e-102.question: What does the Arabic word كَتَبَ (pronounced kataba) mean?
msa-e-102.explanation: كَتَبَ (kataba) means “he wrote”. Practical example: ‘kataba ar-risālah’ (he wrote the letter / كتب الرسالة).

msa-e-103.question: What does the Arabic word نَامَ (pronounced nāma) mean?
msa-e-103.explanation: نَامَ (nāma) means “he slept”. Practical example: ‘nāma mubakkiran’ (he slept early / نام مبكراً).

msa-e-104.question: What does the Arabic word جَلَسَ (pronounced jalasa) mean?
msa-e-104.explanation: جَلَسَ (jalasa) means “he sat”. Practical example: ‘jalasa ʿalā al-kursī’ (he sat on the chair / جلس على الكرسي).

msa-e-105.question: What does the Arabic word وَقَفَ (pronounced waqafa) mean?
msa-e-105.explanation: وَقَفَ (waqafa) means “he stood”. Practical example: ‘waqafa ʿindā al-bāb’ (he stood at the door / وقف عند الباب).

msa-e-106.question: What does the Arabic word مَشَى (pronounced mashā) mean?
msa-e-106.explanation: مَشَى (mashā) means “he walked”. Practical example: ‘mashā ilā al-masjid’ (he walked to the mosque / مشى إلى المسجد).

msa-e-107.question: What does the Arabic word رَكِضَ (pronounced rakaḍa) mean?
msa-e-107.explanation: رَكِضَ (rakaḍa) means “he ran”. Practical example: ‘rakaḍa bi-surʿah’ (he ran quickly / ركض بسرعة).

msa-e-108.question: What does the Arabic word فَتَحَ (pronounced fataḥa) mean?
msa-e-108.explanation: فَتَحَ (fataḥa) means “he opened”. Practical example: ‘fataḥa al-bāb’ (he opened the door / فتح الباب).

msa-e-109.question: What does the Arabic word أَغْلَقَ (pronounced aghlaqa) mean?
msa-e-109.explanation: أَغْلَقَ (aghlaqa) means “he closed”. Practical example: ‘aghlaqa an-nāfidhah’ (he closed the window / أغلق النافذة).

msa-e-110.question: What does the Arabic word دَخَلَ (pronounced dakhala) mean?
msa-e-110.explanation: دَخَلَ (dakhala) means “he entered”. Practical example: ‘dakhala al-bayt’ (he entered the house / دخل البيت).

msa-e-111.question: What does the Arabic word خَرَجَ (pronounced kharaja) mean?
msa-e-111.explanation: خَرَجَ (kharaja) means “he exited” or “left”. Practical example: ‘kharaja min al-madrasah’ (he left the school / خرج من المدرسة).

msa-e-112.question: What does the Arabic word اِشْتَرَى (pronounced ishtarā) mean?
msa-e-112.explanation: اِشْتَرَى (ishtarā) means “he bought”. Practical example: ‘ishtarā kitāban jadīdan’ (he bought a new book / اشترى كتاباً جديداً).

msa-e-113.question: What does the Arabic word بَاعَ (pronounced bāʿa) mean?
msa-e-113.explanation: بَاعَ (bāʿa) means “he sold”. Practical example: ‘bāʿa as-sayyārah’ (he sold the car / باع السيارة).

msa-e-114.question: What does the Arabic word سَأَلَ (pronounced saʾala) mean?
msa-e-114.explanation: سَأَلَ (saʾala) means “he asked”. Practical example: ‘saʾala ʿan aṭ-ṭarīq’ (he asked about the way / سأل عن الطريق).

msa-e-115.question: What does the Arabic word أَجَابَ (pronounced ajāba) mean?
msa-e-115.explanation: أَجَابَ (ajāba) means “he answered”. Practical example: ‘ajāba ʿan as-suʾāl’ (he answered the question / أجاب عن السؤال).

msa-e-116.question: What does the Arabic word قَالَ (pronounced qāla) mean?
msa-e-116.explanation: قَالَ (qāla) means “he said”. Practical example: ‘qāla as-salāmu ʿalaykum’ (he said peace be upon you / قال السلام عليكم).

msa-e-117.question: What does the Arabic word سَمِعَ (pronounced samiʿa) mean?
msa-e-117.explanation: سَمِعَ (samiʿa) means “he heard”. Practical example: ‘samiʿa al-khabar’ (he heard the news / سمع الخبر).

msa-e-118.question: What does the Arabic word رَأَى (pronounced raʾā) mean?
msa-e-118.explanation: رَأَى (raʾā) means “he saw”. Practical example: ‘raʾā al-qamar’ (he saw the moon / رأى القمر).

msa-e-119.question: What does the Arabic word عَرَفَ (pronounced ʿarafa) mean?
msa-e-119.explanation: عَرَفَ (ʿarafa) means “he knew” or “recognised”. Practical example: ‘ʿarafa aṭ-ṭarīq’ (he knew the way / عرف الطريق).

msa-e-120.question: What does the Arabic word تَعَلَّمَ (pronounced taʿallama) mean?
msa-e-120.explanation: تَعَلَّمَ (taʿallama) means “he learned”. Practical example: ‘taʿallama al-ʿarabiyyah’ (he learned Arabic / تعلم العربية).

msa-e-121.question: What does the Arabic word دَرَسَ (pronounced darasa) mean?
msa-e-121.explanation: دَرَسَ (darasa) means “he studied”. Practical example: ‘darasa aṭ-ṭibb’ (he studied medicine / درس الطب).

msa-e-122.question: What does the Arabic word عَمِلَ (pronounced ʿamila) mean?
msa-e-122.explanation: عَمِلَ (ʿamila) means “he worked” or “did”. Practical example: ‘ʿamila bi-jidd’ (he worked hard / عمل بجد).

msa-e-123.question: What does the Arabic word لَعِبَ (pronounced laʿiba) mean?
msa-e-123.explanation: لَعِبَ (laʿiba) means “he played”. Practical example: ‘laʿiba kurat al-qadam’ (he played football / لعب كرة القدم).

msa-e-124.question: What does the Arabic word أَحَبَّ (pronounced aḥabba) mean?
msa-e-124.explanation: أَحَبَّ (aḥabba) means “he loved” or “liked”. Practical example: ‘aḥabba al-qirāʾah’ (he loved reading / أحب القراءة).

msa-e-125.question: What does the Arabic word صَبَاح (pronounced ṣabāḥ) mean?
msa-e-125.explanation: صَبَاح (ṣabāḥ) means “morning”. Practical example: ‘fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ adhhabu ilā al-ʿamal’ (in the morning I go to work / في الصباح أذهب إلى العمل).

msa-e-126.question: What does the Arabic word مَسَاء (pronounced masāʾ) mean?
msa-e-126.explanation: مَسَاء (masāʾ) means “evening”. Practical example: ‘fī al-masāʾ narjaʿu ilā al-bayt’ (in the evening we return home / في المساء نرجع إلى البيت).

msa-e-127.question: What does the Arabic word لَيْل (pronounced layl) mean?
msa-e-127.explanation: لَيْل (layl) means “night”. Practical example: ‘al-laylu ṭawīl fī ash-shitāʾ’ (the night is long in winter / الليل طويل في الشتاء).

msa-e-128.question: What does the Arabic word يَوْم (pronounced yawm) mean?
msa-e-128.explanation: يَوْم (yawm) means “day”. Practical example: ‘al-yawmu jamīl’ (today is beautiful / اليوم جميل).

msa-e-129.question: What does the Arabic word أَمْس (pronounced ams) mean?
msa-e-129.explanation: أَمْس (ams) means “yesterday”. Practical example: ‘jiʾtu ams’ (I came yesterday / جئت أمس).

msa-e-130.question: What does the Arabic word الآن (pronounced al-ān) mean?
msa-e-130.explanation: الآن (al-ān) means “now”. Practical example: ‘anā mashghūlun al-ān’ (I am busy now / أنا مشغول الآن).

msa-e-131.question: What does the Arabic word هُنَا (pronounced hunā) mean?
msa-e-131.explanation: هُنَا (hunā) means “here”. Practical example: ‘taʿāla hunā’ (come here / تعال هنا).

msa-e-132.question: What does the Arabic word هُنَاك (pronounced hunāk) mean?
msa-e-132.explanation: هُنَاك (hunāk) means “there”. Practical example: ‘al-kitābu hunāk’ (the book is there / الكتاب هناك).

msa-e-133.question: What does the Arabic word أَيْن (pronounced ayn) mean?
msa-e-133.explanation: أَيْن (ayn) means “where”. Practical example: ‘ayna al-masjid?’ (Where is the mosque? / أين المسجد؟).

msa-e-134.question: What does the Arabic word مَاذَا (pronounced mādhā) mean?
msa-e-134.explanation: مَاذَا (mādhā) means “what”. Practical example: ‘mādhā taqūlu?’ (What are you saying? / ماذا تقول؟).

msa-e-135.question: What does the Arabic word مَن (pronounced man) mean?
msa-e-135.explanation: مَن (man) means “who”. Practical example: ‘man hādhā?’ (Who is this? / من هذا؟).

msa-e-136.question: What does the Arabic word كَيْف (pronounced kayf) mean?
msa-e-136.explanation: كَيْف (kayf) means “how”. Practical example: ‘kayfa ḥāluka?’ (How are you? / كيف حالك؟).

msa-e-137.question: What does the Arabic word كَمْ (pronounced kam) mean?
msa-e-137.explanation: كَمْ (kam) means “how much” or “how many”. Practical example: ‘kam as-siʿr?’ (How much is the price? / كم السعر؟).

msa-e-138.question: What does the Arabic word نَافِذَة (pronounced nāfidhah) mean?
msa-e-138.explanation: نَافِذَة (nāfidhah) means “window”. Practical example: ‘iftaḥ an-nāfidhah’ (open the window / افتح النافذة).

msa-e-139.question: What does the Arabic word كُرْسِيّ (pronounced kursiyy) mean?
msa-e-139.explanation: كُرْسِيّ (kursiyy) means “chair”. Practical example: ‘ijlis ʿalā al-kursiyy’ (sit on the chair / اجلس على الكرسي).

msa-e-140.question: What does the Arabic word طَاوِلَة (pronounced ṭāwilah) mean?
msa-e-140.explanation: طَاوِلَة (ṭāwilah) means “table”. Practical example: ‘al-kitābu ʿalā aṭ-ṭāwilah’ (the book is on the table / الكتاب على الطاولة).

msa-e-141.question: What does the Arabic word سَرِير (pronounced sarīr) mean?
msa-e-141.explanation: سَرِير (sarīr) means “bed”. Practical example: ‘anāmu ʿalā as-sarīr’ (I sleep on the bed / أنام على السرير).

msa-e-142.question: What does the Arabic word مِفْتَاح (pronounced miftāḥ) mean?
msa-e-142.explanation: مِفْتَاح (miftāḥ) means “key”. Practical example: ‘ayna al-miftāḥ?’ (Where is the key? / أين المفتاح؟).

msa-e-143.question: What does the Arabic word هَاتِف (pronounced hātif) mean?
msa-e-143.explanation: هَاتِف (hātif) means “telephone” or “phone”. Practical example: ‘ittasil bil-hātif’ (call on the phone / اتصل بالهاتف).

msa-e-144.question: What does the Arabic word حَاسُوب (pronounced ḥāsūb) mean?
msa-e-144.explanation: حَاسُوب (ḥāsūb) means “computer”. Practical example: ‘aʿmalu ʿalā al-ḥāsūb’ (I work on the computer / أعمل على الحاسوب).

msa-e-145.question: What does the Arabic word كِتَابَة (pronounced kitābah) mean?
msa-e-145.explanation: كِتَابَة (kitābah) means “writing”. Practical example: ‘uḥibbu al-kitābah’ (I love writing / أحب الكتابة).

msa-e-146.question: What does the Arabic word قِرَاءَة (pronounced qirāʾah) mean?
msa-e-146.explanation: قِرَاءَة (qirāʾah) means “reading”. Practical example: ‘al-qirāʾatu mufīdah’ (reading is beneficial / القراءة مفيدة).

msa-e-147.question: What does the Arabic word كَلَام (pronounced kalām) mean?
msa-e-147.explanation: كَلَام (kalām) means “speech” or “talk”. Practical example: ‘kalāmuhu wāḍiḥ’ (his speech is clear / كلامه واضح).

msa-e-148.question: What does the Arabic word صَوْت (pronounced ṣawt) mean?
msa-e-148.explanation: صَوْت (ṣawt) means “voice” or “sound”. Practical example: ‘ṣawtuhu jamīl’ (his voice is beautiful / صوته جميل).

msa-e-149.question: What does the Arabic word صُورَة (pronounced ṣūrah) mean?
msa-e-149.explanation: صُورَة (ṣūrah) means “picture” or “image”. Practical example: ‘hādhī ṣūratun jamīlah’ (this is a beautiful picture / هذه صورة جميلة).

msa-e-150.question: What does the Arabic word لَوْن (pronounced lawn) mean?
msa-e-150.explanation: لَوْن (lawn) means “colour”. Practical example: ‘mā lawnuhu?’ (What is its colour? / ما لونه؟).

msa-e-151.question: What does the Arabic word حَجْم (pronounced ḥajm) mean?
msa-e-151.explanation: حَجْم (ḥajm) means “size”. Practical example: ‘al-ḥajmu kabīr’ (the size is large / الحجم كبير).

msa-e-152.question: What does the Arabic word طَوِيل (pronounced ṭawīl) mean?
msa-e-152.explanation: طَوِيل (ṭawīl) means “tall” or “long”. Practical example: ‘ar-rajulu ṭawīl’ (the man is tall / الرجل طويل).

msa-e-153.question: What does the Arabic word قَصِير (pronounced qaṣīr) mean?
msa-e-153.explanation: قَصِير (qaṣīr) means “short”. Practical example: ‘al-qiṣṣatu qaṣīrah’ (the story is short / القصة قصيرة).

msa-e-154.question: What does the Arabic word وَاسِع (pronounced wāsiʿ) mean?
msa-e-154.explanation: وَاسِع (wāsiʿ) means “wide” or “spacious”. Practical example: ‘al-baytu wāsiʿ’ (the house is spacious / البيت واسع).

msa-e-155.question: What does the Arabic word ضَيِّق (pronounced ḍayyiq) mean?
msa-e-155.explanation: ضَيِّق (ḍayyiq) means “narrow”. Practical example: ‘aṭ-ṭarīqu ḍayyiq’ (the road is narrow / الطريق ضيق).

msa-e-156.question: What does the Arabic word ثَقِيل (pronounced thaqīl) mean?
msa-e-156.explanation: ثَقِيل (thaqīl) means “heavy”. Practical example: ‘al-ḥaqību thaqīl’ (the bag is heavy / الحقيبة ثقيلة).

msa-e-157.question: What does the Arabic word خَفِيف (pronounced khafīf) mean?
msa-e-157.explanation: خَفِيف (khafīf) means “light” (in weight). Practical example: ‘al-ḥaqību khafīf’ (the bag is light / الحقيبة خفيفة).

msa-e-158.question: What does the Arabic word سَرِيع (pronounced sarīʿ) mean?
msa-e-158.explanation: سَرِيع (sarīʿ) means “fast”. Practical example: ‘as-sayyāratu sarīʿah’ (the car is fast / السيارة سريعة).

msa-e-159.question: What does the Arabic word بَطِيء (pronounced baṭīʾ) mean?
msa-e-159.explanation: بَطِيء (baṭīʾ) means “slow”. Practical example: ‘al-qiṭāru baṭīʾ’ (the train is slow / القطار بطيء).

msa-e-160.question: What does the Arabic word قَرِيب (pronounced qarīb) mean?
msa-e-160.explanation: قَرِيب (qarīb) means “near” or “close”. Practical example: ‘al-masjidu qarīb’ (the mosque is near / المسجد قريب).

msa-e-161.question: What does the Arabic word بَعِيد (pronounced baʿīd) mean?
msa-e-161.explanation: بَعِيد (baʿīd) means “far”. Practical example: ‘al-maṭāru baʿīd’ (the airport is far / المطار بعيد).

msa-e-162.question: What does the Arabic word فَوْق (pronounced fawq) mean?
msa-e-162.explanation: فَوْق (fawq) means “above” or “over”. Practical example: ‘aṭ-ṭāʾiratu fawqa as-saḥāb’ (the plane is above the clouds / الطائرة فوق السحاب).

msa-e-163.question: What does the Arabic word تَحْت (pronounced taḥt) mean?
msa-e-163.explanation: تَحْت (taḥt) means “under” or “below”. Practical example: ‘al-kitābu taḥta aṭ-ṭāwilah’ (the book is under the table / الكتاب تحت الطاولة).

msa-e-164.question: What does the Arabic word أَمَام (pronounced amām) mean?
msa-e-164.explanation: أَمَام (amām) means “in front of”. Practical example: ‘al-masjidu amāma al-bayt’ (the mosque is in front of the house / المسجد أمام البيت).

msa-e-165.question: What does the Arabic word خَلْف (pronounced khalf) mean?
msa-e-165.explanation: خَلْف (khalf) means “behind”. Practical example: ‘al-ḥadīqatu khalfa al-bayt’ (the garden is behind the house / الحديقة خلف البيت).

msa-e-166.question: What does the Arabic word بَيْن (pronounced bayn) mean?
msa-e-166.explanation: بَيْن (bayn) means “between”. Practical example: ‘al-kitābu bayna al-qalamayn’ (the book is between the two pens / الكتاب بين القلمين).

msa-e-167.question: What does the Arabic word دَاخِل (pronounced dākhil) mean?
msa-e-167.explanation: دَاخِل (dākhil) means “inside”. Practical example: ‘ad-darsu dākhila al-faṣl’ (the lesson is inside the classroom / الدرس داخل الفصل).

msa-i-1.question: What does the Arabic word جَامِعَة (pronounced jāmiʿah) mean?
msa-i-1.explanation: جَامِعَة (jāmiʿah) means “University”. Jami'ah (جامعة) means university. Practical example: 'Adrusu al-handasah fi al-jami'ah' (I study engineering at the university / أدرس الهندسة في الجامعة).

msa-i-2.question: What does the Arabic word أَفْهَمُ (pronounced afhamu) mean?
msa-i-2.explanation: أَفْهَمُ (afhamu) means “I understand”. Afhamu (أفهم) means I understand. Practical example: 'Na'am, afhamu ma taquluhu' (Yes, I understand what you are saying / نعم، أفهم ما تقوله).

msa-i-3.question: What does the Arabic word يَكْتُبُ (pronounced yaktubu) mean?
msa-i-3.explanation: يَكْتُبُ (yaktubu) means “He writes”. Yaktubu means he writes. Practical example: 'Al-talibu yaktubu al-dars' (The student writes the lesson / الطالب يكتب الدرس).

msa-i-4.question: What does the Arabic word مَطَار (pronounced maṭār) mean?
msa-i-4.explanation: مَطَار (maṭār) means “Airport”. Matar (مطار) means airport. Practical example: 'Wasalna ila al-matar qabla qalil' (We arrived at the airport a little while ago / وصلنا إلى المطار قبل قليل).

msa-i-5.question: What does the Arabic word فِي رَأْيِي (pronounced fī raʾyī) mean?
msa-i-5.explanation: فِي رَأْيِي (fī raʾyī) means “In my opinion”. Fi ra'yi (في رأيي) means in my opinion. Practical example: 'Fi ra'yi, hadha huwa al-hall al-afdal' (In my opinion, this is the best solution / في رأيي، هذا هو الحل الأفضل).

msa-i-6.question: What does the Arabic word مُسْتَشْفَى (pronounced mustashfā) mean?
msa-i-6.explanation: مُسْتَشْفَى (mustashfā) means “Hospital”. Mustashfa means hospital. Practical example: 'Naqalu al-marid ila al-mustashfa' (They took the patient to the hospital / نقلوا المريض إلى المستشفى).

msa-i-7.question: What does the Arabic word جَرِيدَة (pronounced jarīdah) mean?
msa-i-7.explanation: جَرِيدَة (jarīdah) means “Newspaper”. Jaridah or Sahifah (جريدة / صحيفة) means newspaper. Practical example: 'Aqra'u al-jaridah kulla sabah' (I read the newspaper every morning / أقرأ الجريدة كل صباح).

msa-i-8.question: What does the Arabic word دَائِمًا (pronounced dāʾiman) mean?
msa-i-8.explanation: دَائِمًا (dāʾiman) means “Always”. Daiman (دائماً) means always. Practical example: 'Huwa muta'akhkhirun daiman' (He is always late / هو متأخر دائماً).

msa-i-9.question: What does the Arabic word سَفَر (pronounced safar) mean?
msa-i-9.explanation: سَفَر (safar) means “Travel / Journey”. Safar means travel. Practical example: 'Ista'addu lil-safar ghadan' (Prepare for travel tomorrow / استعدوا للسفر غداً).

msa-i-10.question: What does the Arabic word عَمَل (pronounced ʿamal) mean?
msa-i-10.explanation: عَمَل (ʿamal) means “Work / Job”. Amal or Shughl (عمل / شغل) means work. Practical example: 'Uhibbu amali kithiran' (I love my work very much / أحب عملي كثيراً).

msa-i-11.question: What does the Arabic word أَحْيَانًا (pronounced aḥyānan) mean?
msa-i-11.explanation: أَحْيَانًا (aḥyānan) means “Sometimes”. Ahyanan (أحياناً) means sometimes. Practical example: 'Ahyanan uzuru al-qaryah' (Sometimes I visit the village / أحياناً أزور القرية).

msa-i-12.question: What does the Arabic word مُشْكِلَة (pronounced mushkilah) mean?
msa-i-12.explanation: مُشْكِلَة (mushkilah) means “Problem”. Mushkilah means problem. Practical example: 'Hal ladayka ayyu mushkilah?' (Do you have any problem? / هل لديك أي مشكلة?).

msa-i-13.question: What does the Arabic word حَلّ (pronounced ḥall) mean?
msa-i-13.explanation: حَلّ (ḥall) means “Solution”. Hall (حل) means solution. Practical example: 'Wajadna halla lil-mushkilah' (We found a solution to the problem / وجدنا حلاً للمشكلة).

msa-i-14.question: What does the Arabic word لِمَاذَا؟ (pronounced limādhā) mean?
msa-i-14.explanation: لِمَاذَا؟ (limādhā) means “Why?”. Limadha (لماذا؟) means why. Practical example: 'Limadha ta'akhkharta 'an al-ijtima'?' (Why were you late for the meeting? / لماذا تأخرت عن الاجتماع?).

msa-i-15.question: What does the Arabic word مَتَى (pronounced matā) mean?
msa-i-15.explanation: مَتَى (matā) means “When”. Matta means when. Practical example: 'Matta satansurufu ila al-bayt?' (When will you leave for home? / متى ستنصرف إلى البيت?).

msa-i-16.question: What does the Arabic word مَال / نُقُود (pronounced māl / nuqūd) mean?
msa-i-16.explanation: مَال / نُقُود (māl / nuqūd) means “Money”. Mal or Nuqud (مال / نقود) means money. Practical example: 'Ihtaju ila ba'd al-nuqud' (I need some money / أحتاج إلى بعض النقود).

msa-i-17.question: What does the Arabic word مُهِمّ (pronounced muhimm) mean?
msa-i-17.explanation: مُهِمّ (muhimm) means “Important”. Muhimm (مهم) means important. Practical example: 'Hadha amrun muhimm jiddan' (This is a very important matter / هذا أمر مهم جداً).

msa-i-18.question: What does the Arabic word صَعْب (pronounced ṣaʿb) mean?
msa-i-18.explanation: صَعْب (ṣaʿb) means “Difficult / Hard”. Sa'b means difficult. Practical example: 'Al-imتحان kana sa'ban' (The exam was difficult / الامتحان كان صعباً).

msa-i-19.question: What does the Arabic word سَهْل (pronounced sahl) mean?
msa-i-19.explanation: سَهْل (sahl) means “Easy”. Sahl (سهل) means easy. Practical example: 'Al-lughah al-arabiyyah laysat sahlatun walakinha mumtiah' (The Arabic language is not easy, but it is enjoyable / اللغة العربية ليست سهلة ولكنها ممتعة).

msa-i-20.question: What does the Arabic word سَرِيعًا (pronounced sarīʿan) mean?
msa-i-20.explanation: سَرِيعًا (sarīʿan) means “Fast / Quickly”. Sari'an (سريعاً) means quickly. Practical example: 'Imsi sari'an fa-al-waqtu yatamadda' (Walk quickly, for time is running out / امشِ سريعاً فالوقت يمتد).

msa-i-21.question: What does the Arabic word قَدِيم (pronounced qadīm) mean?
msa-i-21.explanation: قَدِيم (qadīm) means “Old”. Qadeem means old. Practical example: 'Zurna madinah qadimah' (We visited an old city / زرنا مدينة قديمة).

msa-i-22.question: What does the Arabic word جَدِيد (pronounced jadīd) mean?
msa-i-22.explanation: جَدِيد (jadīd) means “New”. Jadeed (جديد) means new. Practical example: 'Ishtaraytu hatifan jadeedan' (I bought a new phone / اشتريت هاتفاً جديداً).

msa-i-23.question: What does the Arabic word أَوَّلًا (pronounced awwalan) mean?
msa-i-23.explanation: أَوَّلًا (awwalan) means “First / Firstly”. Awwalan (أولاً) means first / firstly. Practical example: 'Awwalan, yajibu al-taallum' (Firstly, one must learn / أولاً، يجب التعلم).

msa-i-24.question: What does the Arabic word أَخِيرًا (pronounced akhīran) mean?
msa-i-24.explanation: أَخِيرًا (akhīran) means “Finally / Lastly”. Akheeran means finally. Practical example: 'Wasalna ila al-qimmah akheeran' (We reached the peak finally / وصلنا إلى القمة أخيراً).

msa-i-25.question: What does the Arabic word اِجْتِمَاع (pronounced ijtimāʿ) mean?
msa-i-25.explanation: Ijtima' (اجتماع) means meeting. Practical example: 'Ladayya ijtima' ma' al-mudeer' (I have a meeting with the manager / لدي اجتماع مع المدير).

msa-i-26.question: What does the Arabic word أَعْتَقِدُ / أَظُنُّ (pronounced aʿtaqidu / aẓunnu) mean?
msa-i-26.explanation: أَعْتَقِدُ / أَظُنُّ (aʿtaqidu / aẓunnu) means “I think / I believe”. A'tiqu or Azunnu (أعتقد / أظن) means I think. Practical example: 'Azunnu anna al-matara sayansilu' (I think that it will rain / أظن أن المطر سينزل).

msa-i-27.question: What does the Arabic word مُتَحَدِّث / فَصِيح (pronounced mutaḥaddith / faṣīḥ) mean?
msa-i-27.explanation: مُتَحَدِّث / فَصِيح (mutaḥaddith / faṣīḥ) means “Speaker / Fluent person”. Mutahaddith (متحدث) means speaker. Practical example: 'Huwa mutahaddith bari' bil-lughah al-arabiyyah' (He is a fluent speaker in Arabic / هو متحدث بارع باللغة العربية).

msa-i-28.question: What does the Arabic word شَرِكَة (pronounced sharika) mean?
msa-i-28.explanation: شَرِكَة (sharika) means “Company / Corporation”. Sharikah (شركة) means company. Practical example: 'A'malu fi sharikah kubra' (I work in a major company / أعمل في شركة كبرى).

msa-i-29.question: What does the Arabic word بِلَا / بِدُون (pronounced bilā / bidūn) mean?
msa-i-29.explanation: بِلَا / بِدُون (bilā / bidūn) means “Without”. Bila or Bidun (بلا / بدون) means without. Practical example: 'La yumkinu al-najah bila 'amal' (Success is not possible without work / لا يمكن النجاح بدون عمل).

msa-i-30.question: What does the Arabic word تِجَارَة (pronounced tijārah) mean?
msa-i-30.explanation: تِجَارَة (tijārah) means “Trade / Commerce”. Tijarah means commerce or trade. Practical example: 'Ya'malu fi al-tijarah wal-a'mal' (He works in trade and business / يعمل في التجارة والأعمال).

msa-i-31.question: What does the Arabic word اِقْتِصَاد (pronounced iqtiṣād) mean?
msa-i-31.explanation: Iqtisad (اقتصاد) means economy. Practical example: 'Yadrusu al-iqtisad al-duwali' (He studies international economics / يدرس الاقتصاد الدولي).

msa-i-32.question: What does the Arabic word ثَقَافَة (pronounced thaqāfah) mean?
msa-i-32.explanation: ثَقَافَة (thaqāfah) means “Culture”. Thaqafah (ثقافة) means culture. Practical example: 'Al-thaqafah al-arabiyyah ghaniyyah bil-adab' (Arab culture is rich in literature / الثقافة العربية غنية بالأدب).

msa-i-33.question: What does the Arabic word مُسْتَقْبَل (pronounced mustaqbal) mean?
msa-i-33.explanation: مُسْتَقْبَل (mustaqbal) means “Future”. Mustaqbal means future. Practical example: 'Nabtaniu al-mustaqbal bi-a'malina' (We build the future with our actions / نبني المستقبل بأعمالنا).

msa-i-34.question: What does the Arabic word قِطَار (pronounced qiṭār) mean?
msa-i-34.explanation: قِطَار (qiṭār) means “train”. Practical example: ‘sa-usāfiru bil-qiṭār’ (I will travel by train / سأسافر بالقطار).

msa-i-35.question: What does the Arabic word حَافِلَة (pronounced ḥāfilah) mean?
msa-i-35.explanation: حَافِلَة (ḥāfilah) means “bus”. Practical example: ‘rakkibtu al-ḥāfilah’ (I took the bus / ركبت الحافلة).

msa-i-36.question: What does the Arabic word طَائِرَة (pronounced ṭāʾirah) mean?
msa-i-36.explanation: طَائِرَة (ṭāʾirah) means “airplane”. Practical example: ‘al-ṭāʾiratu taṭīru’ (the plane is flying / الطائرة تطير).

msa-i-37.question: What does the Arabic word سَفِينَة (pronounced safīnah) mean?
msa-i-37.explanation: سَفِينَة (safīnah) means “ship”. Practical example: ‘as-safīnatu kabīrah’ (the ship is large / السفينة كبيرة).

msa-i-38.question: What does the Arabic word تَذْكَرَة (pronounced tadhkirah) mean?
msa-i-38.explanation: تَذْكَرَة (tadhkirah) means “ticket”. Practical example: ‘ishtaraytu tadhkiratan’ (I bought a ticket / اشتريت تذكرة).

msa-i-39.question: What does the Arabic word جَوَاز سَفَر (pronounced jawāz safar) mean?
msa-i-39.explanation: جَوَاز سَفَر (jawāz safar) means “passport”. Practical example: ‘ayna jawāzu safarī?’ (Where is my passport? / أين جواز سفري؟).

msa-i-40.question: What does the Arabic word تَأْشِيرَة (pronounced taʾshīrah) mean?
msa-i-40.explanation: تَأْشِيرَة (taʾshīrah) means “visa”. Practical example: ‘ḥaṣaltu ʿalā taʾshīrah’ (I obtained a visa / حصلت على تأشيرة).

msa-i-41.question: What does the Arabic word مَحَطَّة (pronounced maḥaṭṭah) mean?
msa-i-41.explanation: مَحَطَّة (maḥaṭṭah) means “station”. Practical example: ‘maḥaṭṭat al-qiṭār’ (the train station / محطة القطار).

msa-i-42.question: What does the Arabic word طَرِيق (pronounced ṭarīq) mean?
msa-i-42.explanation: طَرِيق (ṭarīq) means “road” or “way”. Practical example: ‘aṭ-ṭarīqu ṭawīl’ (the road is long / الطريق طويل).

msa-i-43.question: What does the Arabic word جِسْر (pronounced jisr) mean?
msa-i-43.explanation: جِسْر (jisr) means “bridge”. Practical example: ‘ʿabarnā al-jisr’ (we crossed the bridge / عبرنا الجسر).

msa-i-44.question: What does the Arabic word طَبِيب (pronounced ṭabīb) mean?
msa-i-44.explanation: طَبِيب (ṭabīb) means “doctor”. Practical example: ‘dhahabtu ilā aṭ-ṭabīb’ (I went to the doctor / ذهبت إلى الطبيب).

msa-i-45.question: What does the Arabic word مُمَرِّضَة (pronounced mumarriḍah) mean?
msa-i-45.explanation: مُمَرِّضَة (mumarriḍah) means “nurse” (female). Practical example: ‘al-mumarriḍah laṭīfah’ (the nurse is kind / الممرضة لطيفة).

msa-i-46.question: What does the Arabic word مَرِيض (pronounced marīḍ) mean?
msa-i-46.explanation: مَرِيض (marīḍ) means “patient” or “sick person”. Practical example: ‘al-marīḍu yanāmu’ (the patient is sleeping / المريض ينام).

msa-i-47.question: What does the Arabic word دَوَاء (pronounced dawāʾ) mean?
msa-i-47.explanation: دَوَاء (dawāʾ) means “medicine”. Practical example: ‘akhadhtu ad-dawāʾ’ (I took the medicine / أخذت الدواء).

msa-i-48.question: What does the Arabic word وَجَع (pronounced wajaʿ) mean?
msa-i-48.explanation: وَجَع (wajaʿ) means “pain” or “ache”. Practical example: ‘ʿindī wajaʿu raʾs’ (I have a headache / عندي وجع رأس).

msa-i-49.question: What does the Arabic word حُمَّى (pronounced ḥummā) mean?
msa-i-49.explanation: حُمَّى (ḥummā) means “fever”. Practical example: ‘ʿindahu ḥummā’ (he has a fever / عنده حمى).

msa-i-50.question: What does the Arabic word سُعَال (pronounced suʿāl) mean?
msa-i-50.explanation: سُعَال (suʿāl) means “cough”. Practical example: ‘ʿindī suʿāl shadīd’ (I have a strong cough / عندي سعال شديد).

msa-i-51.question: What does the Arabic word صَيْدَلِيَّة (pronounced ṣaydaliyyah) mean?
msa-i-51.explanation: صَيْدَلِيَّة (ṣaydaliyyah) means “pharmacy”. Practical example: ‘ishtaraytu ad-dawāʾ min aṣ-ṣaydaliyyah’ (I bought the medicine from the pharmacy / اشتريت الدواء من الصيدلية).

msa-i-52.question: What does the Arabic word عِلَاج (pronounced ʿilāj) mean?
msa-i-52.explanation: عِلَاج (ʿilāj) means “treatment” or “cure”. Practical example: ‘al-ʿilāju nājiḥ’ (the treatment is successful / العلاج ناجح).

msa-i-53.question: What does the Arabic word صِحَّة (pronounced ṣiḥḥah) mean?
msa-i-53.explanation: صِحَّة (ṣiḥḥah) means “health”. Practical example: ‘aṣ-ṣiḥḥatu muhimmah’ (health is important / الصحة مهمة).

msa-i-54.question: What does the Arabic word دَرْس (pronounced dars) mean?
msa-i-54.explanation: دَرْس (dars) means “lesson”. Practical example: ‘fahimtu ad-dars’ (I understood the lesson / فهمت الدرس).

msa-i-55.question: What does the Arabic word وَاجِب (pronounced wājib) mean?
msa-i-55.explanation: وَاجِب (wājib) means “homework” or “duty”. Practical example: ‘katabtu al-wājib’ (I wrote the homework / كتبت الواجب).

msa-i-56.question: What does the Arabic word اِمْتِحَان (pronounced imtiḥān) mean?
msa-i-56.explanation: اِمْتِحَان (imtiḥān) means “exam” or “test”. Practical example: ‘al-imtiḥānu ṣaʿb’ (the exam is difficult / الامتحان صعب).

msa-i-57.question: What does the Arabic word دَرَجَة (pronounced darajah) mean?
msa-i-57.explanation: دَرَجَة (darajah) means “grade”, “degree” or “temperature”. Practical example: ‘ḥaṣaltu ʿalā darajah ʿāliyah’ (I got a high grade / حصلت على درجة عالية).

msa-i-58.question: What does the Arabic word مُعَلِّمَة (pronounced muʿallimah) mean?
msa-i-58.explanation: مُعَلِّمَة (muʿallimah) means “female teacher”. Practical example: ‘al-muʿallimah sharḥat ad-dars’ (the teacher explained the lesson / المعلمة شرحت الدرس).

msa-i-59.question: What does the Arabic word طَالِبَة (pronounced ṭālibah) mean?
msa-i-59.explanation: طَالِبَة (ṭālibah) means “female student”. Practical example: ‘aṭ-ṭālibah mujtahidah’ (the student is hardworking / الطالبة مجتهدة).

msa-i-60.question: What does the Arabic word كُلِّيَّة (pronounced kulliyyah) mean?
msa-i-60.explanation: كُلِّيَّة (kulliyyah) means “college” or “faculty”. Practical example: ‘kulliyyat aṭ-ṭibb’ (the faculty of medicine / كلية الطب).

msa-i-61.question: What does the Arabic word مَكْتَبَة (pronounced maktabah) mean?
msa-i-61.explanation: مَكْتَبَة (maktabah) means “library”. Practical example: ‘aqraʾu fī al-maktabah’ (I read in the library / أقرأ في المكتبة).

msa-i-62.question: What does the Arabic word قَامُوس (pronounced qāmūs) mean?
msa-i-62.explanation: قَامُوس (qāmūs) means “dictionary”. Practical example: ‘baḥathtu fī al-qāmūs’ (I searched in the dictionary / بحثت في القاموس).

msa-i-63.question: What does the Arabic word مَجَلَّة (pronounced majallah) mean?

msa-i-65.question: What does the Arabic word مُحَامٍ (pronounced muḥāmin) mean?

msa-i-66.question: What does the Arabic word صَحَفِيّ (pronounced ṣaḥafiyy) mean?

msa-i-67.question: What does the Arabic word طَبَّاخ (pronounced ṭabbākh) mean?

msa-i-68.question: What does the Arabic word شُرْطِيّ (pronounced shurṭiyy) mean?
msa-i-68.explanation: شُرْطِيّ (shurṭiyy) means “police officer”. Practical example: ‘ash-shurṭiyyu yunẓimu al-murūr’ (the officer directs traffic / الشرطي ينظم المرور).

msa-i-69.question: What does the Arabic word فَلَّاح (pronounced fallāḥ) mean?

msa-i-70.question: What does the Arabic word تَاجِر (pronounced tājir) mean?

msa-i-71.question: What does the Arabic word مُوَظَّف (pronounced muwaẓẓaf) mean?

msa-i-72.question: What does the Arabic word مُدِير (pronounced mudīr) mean?
msa-i-72.explanation: مُدِير (mudīr) means “manager” or “director”. Practical example: ‘al-mudīru ʿaqada ijtimāʿan’ (the manager held a meeting / المدير عقد اجتماعاً).

msa-i-73.question: What does the Arabic word رَاتِب (pronounced rātib) mean?

msa-i-74.question: What does the Arabic word سِعْر (pronounced siʿr) mean?

msa-i-76.question: What does the Arabic word غَالٍ (pronounced ghālin) mean?

msa-i-81.question: What does the Arabic word عُمْلَة (pronounced ʿumlah) mean?

msa-i-84.question: What does the Arabic word شَجَرَة (pronounced shajarah) mean?

msa-i-119.question: What does the Arabic word اِنْتَهَى (pronounced intahā) mean?
